newsitem.title: MEXICO: Mexico peso strong on structural factors - cenbank.
newsitem.headline: Mexico peso strong on structural factors - cenbank.

text.p: A deputy governor of Banco de Mexico, Guillermo Guemez, said on Friday that structural factors were behind the recent strength of the Mexican peso.
Speaking at the National Convention of the Foreign Exchange Association, Guemez said that direct foreign investment and other foreign financing was keeping the peso strong.
"These structural factors are mainly direct foreign investment for one side, and on the other, Mexican businesses are being substantially financed by foreign money," he said.
The central bank has been criticized recently by some businessmen who say the free-floating peso is too strong against the U.S. dollar.
The peso suffered a sharp devaluation in late 1994 which plunged the country into an economic crisis, but it has been slowly gaining strength in real terms since then.
